checked_claims: The directly opened final Opéra-Comique programme identifies Carmen as an opéra-comique in four acts by Georges Bizet, with libretto by Henri Meilhac and Ludovic Halévy after Mérimée, created on 3 March 1875 at Opéra-Comique.
The second directly opened Opéra-Comique page supports the account of source research without travel to Spain and supports Micaëla as an addition by Meilhac and Halévy.
The article correctly separates composer, librettists, literary source, Paris premiere, and Seville setting; it makes no false inference that the setting identifies the premiere country.
items.distractor_review: Verdi, Mozart, and Puccini did not compose Carmen. Bizet is the only best answer; Meilhac and Halévy are correctly described as librettists rather than composers.

checked_claims: La Scala's historical page identifies Otello as created there on 5 February 1887 by Verdi, with Arrigo Boito as librettist, and describes the collaboration with Ricordi and Faccio.
La Scala's Otello page identifies Giuseppe Verdi, Arrigo Boito, and the work's four acts; its 1887 framing matches the article's disambiguating detail.

Royal Ballet and Opera Collections identifies Rossini's separate Otello (1816), names Francesco Berio di Salsa as its librettist, records the 4 December 1816 Naples world premiere, and identifies 6 July 1850 only as that institution's local premiere.
The article correctly distinguishes composer, librettist, work identity, world premiere, and local production history.
items.distractor_review: The date and La Scala premise uniquely identify Verdi. Bizet, Mozart, and Puccini did not compose this Otello; Rossini's earlier 1816 work is a historically useful but explicitly distinct comparator.
